title: Given a circular array of integers where the end wraps around to the beginning, find the maximum sum of any contiguous non-empty subarray, allowing the subarray to wrap around. Solve it with a combination of maximum and minimum Kadane and demonstrate with a complete banking mini-project.

s1_definition.profdef: The maximum circular subarray sum problem asks for the largest sum of any contiguous non-empty subarray in a circular array, where a subarray may wrap from the end back to the start. It is solved with two Kadane passes plus the total sum: the answer is the larger of the ordinary maximum subarray sum, which handles non-wrapping cases, and the total sum minus the minimum subarray sum, which handles wrapping cases by removing the worst middle segment, with a guard for the all-negative array.
s1_definition.analogy: At the National Bank of India, Rajesh looks at a repeating weekly cycle of daily net cash flows that wraps from Sunday back to Monday, and wants the most profitable continuous stretch, which might start late in one week and continue into the next. A wrapping stretch is the whole week minus some unwanted middle slump, so he finds the best non-wrapping stretch the normal way, and separately finds the worst middle slump to carve out, and takes whichever gives more.
s1_definition.oneliner: The best circular sum is the larger of the normal Kadane maximum and the total minus the minimum subarray, guarding the all-negative edge case.
s1_definition.raw:
**Professional definition:** The maximum circular subarray sum problem asks for the largest sum of any contiguous non-empty subarray in a circular array, where a subarray may wrap from the end back to the start. It is solved with two Kadane passes plus the total sum: the answer is the larger of the ordinary maximum subarray sum, which handles non-wrapping cases, and the total sum minus the minimum subarray sum, which handles wrapping cases by removing the worst middle segment, with a guard for the all-negative array.

**In simple words (banking analogy):** At the National Bank of India, Rajesh looks at a repeating weekly cycle of daily net cash flows that wraps from Sunday back to Monday, and wants the most profitable continuous stretch, which might start late in one week and continue into the next. A wrapping stretch is the whole week minus some unwanted middle slump, so he finds the best non-wrapping stretch the normal way, and separately finds the worst middle slump to carve out, and takes whichever gives more.

**One line to remember:** The best circular sum is the larger of the normal Kadane maximum and the total minus the minimum subarray, guarding the all-negative edge case.

sections.s2_technical:
A subarray in a circular array is one of two shapes. Either it does not wrap, in which case it is an ordinary contiguous subarray and the standard maximum Kadane finds the best such sum. Or it does wrap, meaning it includes some suffix of the array joined to some prefix. The clever observation is that a wrapping subarray is exactly the whole array with a contiguous non-wrapping middle segment removed. To maximize the wrapping sum we must remove the middle segment with the smallest sum, so the best wrapping sum equals the total sum minus the minimum subarray sum.

We therefore compute three things in one or two passes: the maximum subarray sum using standard Kadane, the minimum subarray sum using minimum Kadane, and the total of all elements. The answer is `Math.max(maxKadane, total - minKadane)`. The maximum Kadane term covers the non-wrapping case and the total-minus-minimum term covers the wrapping case, and taking the larger of the two gives the global best.

There is one critical edge case that trips up many candidates. If every element is negative, then the minimum subarray sum equals the total sum, so `total - minKadane` becomes zero, which would correspond to removing the entire array and keeping an empty subarray. But the subarray must be non-empty, so zero is invalid here. We detect this by checking whether the maximum Kadane result is negative, which happens exactly when all elements are negative, and in that case we return the maximum Kadane result directly, which is the least-negative single element. The senior-level nuance is precisely this all-negative guard; without it the algorithm silently returns zero and is wrong.

We can compute the maximum, minimum, and total in a single loop to stay efficient. The time complexity is linear, O(n), and the space complexity is O(1). This max-Kadane-plus-total-minus-min-Kadane decomposition, with the all-negative guard, is the standard and expected solution for circular subarray problems.
sections.s3_banking:
Problem 1 — At the National Bank of India, a treasury account operates on a repeating settlement cycle where the daily net cash flows form a circular sequence, the last day of the cycle flowing into the first day of the next. The desk wants the most profitable continuous stretch of days within the cycle, and because the cycle wraps, the best stretch might begin near the end of one cycle and continue into the beginning of the next. This is exactly the maximum sum circular subarray problem.

Problem 2 — Simulating the wrap by duplicating the array and running a windowed search is clumsy and wasteful at the bank's scale. The two-Kadane decomposition finds both the non-wrapping and wrapping best stretches in a single linear pass, with a guard for the all-loss cycle, which makes the periodic cash-cycle analysis efficient.

The code has the shared `Account` class, a `CyclicCashFlowAnalyzer` service with a `bestCyclicStretch` method implementing the decomposition, and a runnable `MaxCircularSubarrayDemo` main class that runs Rajesh's and Priya's circular cash-flow cycles, logging the three computed quantities at fine level and the best cyclic stretch at info level.

sections.s5_journey:
Input data: Rajesh's circular cycle is 5, -3, 5. We seed the running maximum and maximum sum at 5, the running minimum and minimum sum at 5, and the total at 5.

Step 1 at index 1, value -3: total becomes 2. Running maximum is the larger of -3 and 5 plus -3 which is 2, so 2; maximum sum stays 5. Running minimum is the smaller of -3 and 5 plus -3 which is 2, so -3; minimum sum becomes -3.

Step 2 at index 2, value 5: total becomes 7. Running maximum is the larger of 5 and 2 plus 5 which is 7, so 7; maximum sum becomes 7. Running minimum is the smaller of 5 and -3 plus 5 which is 2, so 2; minimum sum stays -3.

Now we combine. The maximum sum is 7, which is not negative, so the all-negative guard does not apply. The wrapping candidate is total minus minimum sum, which is 7 minus -3 equals 10. The answer is the larger of the non-wrapping 7 and the wrapping 10, which is 10.

The best cyclic stretch for Rajesh is 10, the wrapping subarray that takes the 5 at the last index and wraps to the 5 at the first index, skipping the -3 in the middle.

```
2026-10-27 18:52:00 INFO    Rajesh Kumar (SAV2001) cycle
2026-10-27 18:52:00 INFO    Best cyclic stretch over [5, -3, 5] = max(maxSum 7, total 7 - minSum -3) = 10
2026-10-27 18:52:00 INFO    Rajesh Kumar best cyclic stretch = 10
2026-10-27 18:52:00 INFO    Priya Sharma (CUR3001) cycle
2026-10-27 18:52:00 FINE    All-negative cycle; returning best single element
2026-10-27 18:52:00 INFO    Best cyclic stretch over [-2, -3, -1] = max(maxSum -1, total -6 - minSum -6) = -1
2026-10-27 18:52:00 INFO    Priya Sharma best cyclic stretch = -1
```
sections.s5b_flow:
```
  Input: circular cycle [5,-3,5]
    │
    ▼
  CyclicCashFlowAnalyzer.bestCyclicStretch()  (max + min Kadane + total)
    │ seed: curMax=maxSum=5, curMin=minSum=5, total=5
    │
    ├─ i=1 -3: total2 curMax=2 maxSum5 curMin=-3 minSum-3
    └─ i=2  5: total7 curMax=7 maxSum7 curMin=2  minSum-3
    │
    ├─ non-wrap candidate = maxSum = 7
    ├─ wrap candidate     = total - minSum = 7 - (-3) = 10
    └─ maxSum≥0 so no all-negative guard
    │
    ▼
  answer = max(7, 10) = 10  (wrap: last 5 → first 5, skipping -3)
```

sections.s6_takeaway:
The maximum sum circular subarray problem asks for the largest sum of any contiguous non-empty subarray in a circular array where the subarray may wrap from the end back to the start, and I solve it in a single linear pass. The insight is that any subarray is one of two shapes. A non-wrapping subarray is handled by ordinary maximum Kadane. A wrapping subarray is exactly the whole array with a contiguous non-wrapping middle segment removed, so to maximize it I remove the segment with the smallest sum, which means the best wrapping sum is the total of all elements minus the minimum subarray sum.

So I compute three values, the maximum subarray sum, the minimum subarray sum, and the total, and the answer is the larger of the maximum Kadane result and the total minus the minimum Kadane result. The one edge case I always call out is the all-negative array. When every element is negative, the minimum subarray equals the whole array, so total minus minimum becomes zero, which would correspond to an empty subarray, but the subarray must be non-empty. I detect this by checking whether the maximum Kadane result is negative, and if so I return that result directly, the least-negative single element.

In my banking project at the National Bank of India I used this on the treasury desk. A treasury account operated on a repeating settlement cycle where daily net cash flows formed a circular sequence, the last day flowing into the first of the next cycle, and we wanted the most profitable continuous stretch, which could begin near the end of one cycle and continue into the next. The two-Kadane decomposition found both the non-wrapping and wrapping best stretches in one pass with the all-loss guard, which was far cleaner than duplicating the array.

The senior-level point I make is that the wrapping case reduces elegantly to removing the minimum middle segment, which is a reframing that many candidates miss, and that the all-negative guard is the single detail that separates a correct solution from one that silently returns zero. I also mention that I compute the maximum, minimum, and total in one combined loop to keep it a single pass, and that for monetary data I accumulate in a long or BigDecimal against overflow. Explaining the removal reframing and insisting on the all-negative guard is exactly what demonstrates mastery to an interviewer.
